headline: What to Donate, Sell, Store, Recycle, or Throw Away
alternativeHeadline: The fourth and final Sort chapter. The out box is already decided, so today you only route it: five doors out, and most of the box goes through Donate and Recycle.
description: Chapter 11 closes Sort by routing the already-decided out box through five doors, Donate, Sell, Store, Recycle, or Throw. Deciding a thing is unnecessary and deciding where it goes are two separate acts, and only the second remains, so a quick cascade picks each item's door in a second: broken then Recycle or Throw, valuable and worth the work then Sell with a deadline, needed later then Store labeled and dated, still useful then Donate. The bias is deliberate. Donate and Recycle are the fast lanes and take most of the box, while Sell and Store are narrow on purpose, each fenced with a guardrail: a sell-by deadline on selling, a label and date on storing, and never rent space for what you do not need. Donate is the default because it is the exit that actually completes, same day, and donating a usable thing is not waste. Recycle and Throw handle the worn and the finished, with the sunk-cost reframe that the waste, if there ever was any, happened at the store, not at the bin. A short routing pass empties the entryway out box between the two fast doors, and the friction meter takes its last Sort step to a Sort-complete milestone while the goal stays ahead, because five S's remain.
